body:
BATCH 1 IS VERIFIED MERGEABLE. Measured against current main 1a55f19, not assumed.

  337600b  NFRD    docs x2 + embed-bench x4                     merge-tree: clean
  7ee4872  scout   align/hsmm.scala + TransitionFeaturesSuite   merge-tree: clean
  e6d0cc5  m1      align cost+wire, codec/align, laws/Laws,
                   fixtures goldens x4                          merge-tree: clean

  PAIRWISE FILE OVERLAP: NFRD∩scout 0, m1∩NFRD 0, m1∩scout 0. m1 and scout are both in align but
  touch different files.

A CLEAN MERGE-TREE IS NOT A WORKING MERGE and I am not treating it as one -- it says nothing about
whether the types still agree, which is exactly why the single full court exists and why scout's
rebase over a12fdde is still required.

FLAGGING, because it is the largest thing in the batch and it should not arrive unannounced at push
time: BATCH 1 BUMPS THE CODEC SCHEMA. e6d0cc5 changes `SchemaVersion` from "hsmm/v2" to "hsmm/v3" in
codec/align.scala and carries both goldens (hsmm-v2-wog.json retained, hsmm-v3-wog.json added). That
is a compatibility event for any consumer reading our wire format.

IT IS ACCOUNTING-ONLY, AND I VERIFIED THAT MYSELF EARLIER TONIGHT rather than taking it on the
author's word: all 18 golden `total` values are BYTE-IDENTICAL between v2 and v3, and the golden file
grew by exactly 324 bytes -- the size of the added accounting fields and nothing else. NO PRICE
MOVED. That was the "accounting before pricing" ruling and e6d0cc5 honours it: imputedTerms records
what was priced from a constant WITHOUT changing what it was priced at.

REMAINING BEFORE BATCH 1 CAN MERGE:
  NFRD    grok's review (only `review_missing` of the three)
  scout   rebase over a12fdde + align re-run; reviews already satisfied
  m1      rebase onto current main; then it joins

Then one scalafmtCheckAll + compileAll + testAll on the merged tree, exit captured unpiped, totals
verified per module, and codex-storymodel-release pushes -- noting release is EXPIRED, which is
finding 1 from the cross-repo post and now sits on the critical path rather than beside it.
